<p id="A2.p2.7" class="ltx_p">The <math id="A2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z\bar{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>Z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z\bar{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> component of the Einstein equation is satisfied as a
consequence of these equations. The arbitrary function
<math id="A2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{c}(\bar{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>Z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{c}(\bar{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> reflects the freedom to do a coordinate
transformation <math id="A2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{Z}\rightarrow\bar{Z}^{\prime}(\bar{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>Z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>Z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>Z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{Z}\rightarrow\bar{Z}^{\prime}(\bar{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>, and one can
also do a coordinate transformation <math id="A2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z\rightarrow w(Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z\rightarrow w(Z)</annotation></semantics></math> to eliminate
<math id="A2.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(Z)</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence these solutions are characterized by <math id="A2.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-2</annotation></semantics></math> functions <math id="A2.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}(Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}(Z)</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="A2.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-2</annotation></semantics></math> functions <math id="A2.p2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{a}_{i}(\bar{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>Z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{a}_{i}(\bar{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>. However, the constraints
<a href="#A2.E11" title="In Appendix B The special Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.11</span></a> and <a href="#A2.E13" title="In Appendix B The special Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.13</span></a> imply that only <math id="A2.p2.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-4</annotation></semantics></math> of the
functions <math id="A2.p2.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{a}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{a}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> are independent, and the constraint
<a href="#A2.E12" title="In Appendix B The special Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.12</span></a> implies that only <math id="A2.p2.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-3</annotation></semantics></math> of the functions <math id="A2.p2.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> are
independent. For <math id="A2.p2.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=4</annotation></semantics></math>, the solution is given by a single arbitrary
function <math id="A2.p2.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}(Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}(Z)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.p2.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial/\partial\bar{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mo rspace="0.055em">/</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>Z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial/\partial\bar{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> is a null Killing
vector field so the solution describes a pp-wave spacetime
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite>. These solutions admit a Killing spinor
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>. The higher dimensional analogues of these pp-waves are
the solutions with <math id="A2.p2.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{a}_{i}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{a}_{i}=0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.p2.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, and it is
straightforward to show that these are the only Weyl solutions
that satisfy the integrability conditions for the existence of a Killing
spinor.</p>
</div>
</section>

tensor of the metric <a href="#S2.E3" title="In 2.2 Solving the Einstein equations ‣ 2 Generalized Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a> vanishes if, and only if,</p>

<p id="A3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Equation <a href="#A3.E4" title="In Appendix C Weyl forms of flat space" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.4</span></a> can be immediately solved:</p>
<table id="A3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}(Z,\bar{Z})=\log(a_{i}(Z)+a_{i}(Z)^{*})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>Z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}(Z,\bar{Z})=\log(a_{i}(Z)+a_{i}(Z)^{*}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(C.6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}(Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}(Z)</annotation></semantics></math> is arbitrary.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">It is convenient to choose the labelling of the <math id="A3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> such
that <math id="A3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial_{Z}a_{i}\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial_{Z}a_{i}\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq i\leq r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq i\leq r</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial_{Z}a_{i}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial_{Z}a_{i}=0</annotation></semantics></math>
for <math id="A3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i&gt;r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i&gt;r</annotation></semantics></math>. Equation <a href="#A3.E2" title="In Appendix C Weyl forms of flat space" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a> is automatically satisfied if
<math id="A3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i&gt;r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i&gt;r</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j&gt;r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j&gt;r</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="A3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i,j\leq r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i,j\leq r</annotation></semantics></math> then this equation implies</p>
<table id="A3.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial_{Z}a_{i}}{\partial_{Z}a_{j}}=-\frac{(\partial_{Z}a_{i})^{*}}{(\partial_{Z}a_{j})^{*}}=i\lambda_{ij}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial_{Z}a_{i}}{\partial_{Z}a_{j}}=-\frac{(\partial_{Z}a_{i})^{*}}{(\partial_{Z}a_{j})^{*}}=i\lambda_{ij},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(C.7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{ij}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math> is a real non-zero constant.
If <math id="A3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&gt;2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&gt;2</annotation></semantics></math> then it follows that</p>
<table id="A3.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E8.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\partial_{Z}a_{3}=i\lambda_{32}\partial_{Z}a_{2}=-\lambda_{32}\lambda_{21}\partial_{Z}a_{1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>Z</mi></msub><mi>a</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>λ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>32</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em">∂</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>Z</mi></msub><mi>a</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mi>λ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>32</mn></msub><mi>λ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>21</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em">∂</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>Z</mi></msub><mi>a</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial_{Z}a_{3}=i\lambda_{32}\partial_{Z}a_{2}=-\lambda_{32}\lambda_{21}\partial_{Z}a_{1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(C.8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p2.3" class="ltx_p">However, this contradicts <math id="A3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial_{Z}a_{3}=i\lambda_{31}\partial_{Z}a_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>31</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial_{Z}a_{3}=i\lambda_{31}\partial_{Z}a_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence <math id="A3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=0,1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=0,1</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A3.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>. These three cases will be discussed
individually.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=0</annotation></semantics></math> then <math id="A3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}(Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}(Z)</annotation></semantics></math> is a constant for all <math id="A3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> and hence <math id="A3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is
constant for all <math id="A3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. Equations <a href="#A3.E2" title="In Appendix C Weyl forms of flat space" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a> and
<a href="#A3.E3" title="In Appendix C Weyl forms of flat space" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a> are trivially satisfied and equation
<a href="#A3.E5" title="In Appendix C Weyl forms of flat space" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.5</span></a> has the solution</p>
<table id="A3.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C(Z,\bar{Z})=c(Z)+c(Z)^{*}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>Z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(Z,\bar{Z})=c(Z)+c(Z)^{*},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>

</table>
<p id="A3.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c(Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c(Z)</annotation></semantics></math> is arbitrary. This arbitrary function can be eliminated
by a coordinate transformation <math id="A3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z\rightarrow Z^{\prime}(Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z\rightarrow Z^{\prime}(Z)</annotation></semantics></math>. The line element
is then obviously flat.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=1</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> then equations <a href="#A3.E2" title="In Appendix C Weyl forms of flat space" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a> and
<a href="#A3.E3" title="In Appendix C Weyl forms of flat space" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a> are trivially satisfied for <math id="A3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i&gt;r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i&gt;r</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="A3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\leq r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\leq r</annotation></semantics></math>, the
solution is</p>
<table id="A3.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C(Z,\bar{Z})=\frac{1}{2}\log\left(\partial_{Z}a_{i}\right)\left(\partial_{Z}a_{i}\right)^{*}+{\rm constant}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>Z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>constant</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(Z,\bar{Z})=\frac{1}{2}\log\left(\partial_{Z}a_{i}\right)\left(\partial_{Z}a_{i}\right)^{*}+{\rm constant},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(C.10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p4.2" class="ltx_p">which also ensures that equation <a href="#A3.E5" title="In Appendix C Weyl forms of flat space" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.5</span></a> is satisfied. For
<math id="A3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=1</annotation></semantics></math>, after changing coordinates from <math id="A3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1}(Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1}(Z)</annotation></semantics></math>, setting <math id="A3.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1}=\xi+i\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ξ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1}=\xi+i\eta</annotation></semantics></math> and rescaling the coordinates to eliminate constants,
the line element takes the form</p>
<table id="A3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="ds^{2}=\epsilon_{1}\xi^{2}(dx^{1})^{2}+\sum_{i=2}^{D-2}\epsilon_{i}(dx^{i})^{2}+d\xi^{2}+d\eta^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ξ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ξ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ds^{2}=\epsilon_{1}\xi^{2}(dx^{1})^{2}+\sum_{i=2}^{D-2}\epsilon_{i}(dx^{i})^{2}+d\xi^{2}+d\eta^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(C.11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p4.3" class="ltx_p">This line element is
manifestly flat, with <math id="A3.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{1}</annotation></semantics></math> an angular coordinate (if <math id="A3.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{1}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{1}=1</annotation></semantics></math>) or the boost coordinate in Rindler space (if <math id="A3.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{1}=-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{1}=-1</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="A3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=2</annotation></semantics></math>, after changing and rescaling the coordinates as above,
the line element takes the form</p>
<table id="A3.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="ds^{2}=\epsilon_{1}\xi^{2}(dx^{1})^{2}+\epsilon_{2}\eta^{2}(dx^{2})^{2}+\sum_{i=3}^{D-2}\epsilon_{i}(dx^{i})^{2}+d\xi^{2}+d\eta^{2}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ξ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ξ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ds^{2}=\epsilon_{1}\xi^{2}(dx^{1})^{2}+\epsilon_{2}\eta^{2}(dx^{2})^{2}+\sum_{i=3}^{D-2}\epsilon_{i}(dx^{i})^{2}+d\xi^{2}+d\eta^{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(C.12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p5.2" class="ltx_p">which is manifestly flat, with <math id="A3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{1}</annotation></semantics></math> an angular/boost coordinate depending
on the sign of <math id="A3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, and similarly for <math id="A3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p6.1" class="ltx_p">In order to identify the sources terms for Laplace’s equation that
these flat metrics correspond to, one must first change coordinate from
<math id="A3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(Z)</annotation></semantics></math> (defined by equation <a href="#S2.E18" title="In 2.3 Relation to Laplace’s equation ‣ 2 Generalized Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.18</span></a> with <math id="A3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{w}=w^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>w</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>w</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{w}=w^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>). However, this is not possible if <math id="A3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=0</annotation></semantics></math> because then <math id="A3.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math> is
constant. Hence <math id="A3.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=0</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to the special case analyzed in
section <a href="#S2.SS4" title="2.4 Special classes of solutions ‣ 2 Generalized Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p7.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="A3.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is constant for <math id="A3.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math> so equation <a href="#S2.E18" title="In 2.3 Relation to Laplace’s equation ‣ 2 Generalized Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.18</span></a> reduces to</p>
<table id="A3.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{1}=\log(w+\bar{w})+{\rm constant}=\log r+{\rm constant}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>+</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>w</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>constant</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>constant</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{1}=\log(w+\bar{w})+{\rm constant}=\log r+{\rm constant}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(C.13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p7.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w=r+iz" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w=r+iz</annotation></semantics></math>. The constant term can be eliminated by rescaling the
coordinate <math id="A3.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{1}</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="A3.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> is the Newtonian potential produced by an
infinite rod lying on the <math id="A3.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>-axis. The rod has vanishing thickness
and mass <math id="A3.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2</annotation></semantics></math> per unit length.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p8.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="A3.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is constant for <math id="A3.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i&gt;2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i&gt;2</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="A3.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> are given by
equation <a href="#A3.E6" title="In Appendix C Weyl forms of flat space" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.6</span></a>. Recall that <math id="A3.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial_{Z}a_{2}=i\lambda_{21}\partial_{Z}a_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>21</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mi>Z</mi></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial_{Z}a_{2}=i\lambda_{21}\partial_{Z}a_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> hence <math id="A3.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{2}=\lambda_{21}(ia_{1}+c)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>21</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{2}=\lambda_{21}(ia_{1}+c)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A3.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> is a
constant. The imaginary part of <math id="A3.p8.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> does not affect <math id="A3.p8.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> so <math id="A3.p8.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> can
be taken to be real. Equation <a href="#S2.E18" title="In 2.3 Relation to Laplace’s equation ‣ 2 Generalized Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.18</span></a> then gives</p>
<table id="A3.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w+w^{*}\propto[a_{1}+a_{1}^{*}][i(a_{1}-a_{1})^{*}+2c]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>w</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w+w^{*}\propto[a_{1}+a_{1}^{*}][i(a_{1}-a_{1})^{*}+2c],</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<math id="A3.p8.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p8.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math id="A3.p8.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Formulae for the black ring</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In order to write the metric of the black ring in Weyl form, it
turns out to be convenient to look for constants <math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> such that</p>
<table id="A4.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{2}+(z-c/A^{2})^{2}=\frac{1}{4(x-y)^{2}A^{4}}\left(\alpha\mu xy-2cx-2cy+\beta\right)^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{2}+(z-c/A^{2})^{2}=\frac{1}{4(x-y)^{2}A^{4}}\left(\alpha\mu xy-2cx-2cy+\beta\right)^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(D.1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">A priori</span>, one would not expect such constants to exist. However,
it turns out that they do, and are given by</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</table>
<p id="A4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">and</p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(D.3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p1.4" class="ltx_p">The solutions are</p>
<table id="A4.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\beta=\alpha\mu,\,c=\alpha/2,\qquad\beta=\alpha(2-\mu),\,c=\alpha\mu/2,\qquad\beta=-\alpha(2+\mu),\,c=-\alpha\mu/2." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>μ</mi><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>μ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mi>α</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>μ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=\alpha\mu,\,c=\alpha/2,\qquad\beta=\alpha(2-\mu),\,c=\alpha\mu/2,\qquad\beta=-\alpha(2+\mu),\,c=-\alpha\mu/2.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(D.4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p1.5" class="ltx_p">Note that the solutions for <math id="A4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> can be written as <math id="A4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{2}a_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A^{2}a_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, where the
quantities <math id="A4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> were defined in section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 The black ring ‣ 4 New solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>. It follows
that each function <math id="A4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> defined in section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 The black ring ‣ 4 New solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> is
the square root of the right hand side of equation <a href="#A4.E1" title="In Appendix D Formulae for the black ring" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a>
for the appropriate value of <math id="A4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>. Since the right hand side of this
equation is a perfect square, the expressions for <math id="A4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> turn out to be
quite simple:</p>

<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Calculating <math id="A5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math> integrals</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The purpose of this appendix is to explain how the quantity <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math> in
equation <a href="#S2.E17" title="In 2.3 Relation to Laplace’s equation ‣ 2 Generalized Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.17</span></a> is calculated for the solutions of
section <a href="#S4" title="4 New solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. Consider first the solution of section
<a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Superposition of a black hole and KK bubble ‣ 4 New solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>. In terms of the complex coordinates <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math>, the
functions <math id="A5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> take the form</p>

<p id="A5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the constants <math id="A5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> are defined in equation <a href="#S4.E11" title="In 4.3 The black ring ‣ 4 New solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.11</span></a> and
arbitrary additive constants are suppressed. To calculate <math id="A5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math>
directly, these expressions could be substituted into equations
<a href="#S2.E20" title="In 2.3 Relation to Laplace’s equation ‣ 2 Generalized Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.20</span></a> and <a href="#S2.E21" title="In 2.3 Relation to Laplace’s equation ‣ 2 Generalized Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.21</span></a>. On the right hand side of these
equations there would be <math id="A5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12</annotation></semantics></math> terms (<math id="A5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> from each <math id="A5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial U_{i}\partial U_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial U_{i}\partial U_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>).
Alternatively, one can instead deal with <math id="A5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, which is determined
by equations <a href="#S2.E23" title="In 2.3 Relation to Laplace’s equation ‣ 2 Generalized Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.23</span></a> and <a href="#S2.E24" title="In 2.3 Relation to Laplace’s equation ‣ 2 Generalized Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.24</span></a>, with only 10
terms on the right hand side. Having obtained <math id="A5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math> can be
immediately calculated using</p>
<table id="A5.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="A5.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Equation <a href="#S2.E23" title="In 2.3 Relation to Laplace’s equation ‣ 2 Generalized Weyl solutions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.23</span></a> takes the form</p>
<table id="A5.EGx11" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_eqnarray ltx_eqn_table">

<tr class="ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="A5.p1.5" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A5.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> are real constants with <math id="A5.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c&gt;d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c&gt;d</annotation></semantics></math>. integrate equation <a href="#A5.Ex14" title="In Appendix E Calculating 𝜈 integrals" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.5</span></a>, it is necessary to integrate <math id="A5.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="A5.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math>. This can be done by a change of variable to <math id="A5.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z=(c+iw)^{1/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z=(c+iw)^{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math>, which yields</p>

<p id="A5.p1.7" class="ltx_p">These results yield <math id="A5.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, and hence <math id="A5.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math>, up to an arbitrary
function of <math id="A5.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{w}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>w</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{w}</annotation></semantics></math>. This function can be determined up to a real
constant of integration by demanding that <math id="A5.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math> be real. Finally, the
following expressions can be used to express <math id="A5.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math id="A5.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A5.p1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\zeta_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\zeta_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.p1.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{ij}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

      methods listed below:</p>

          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>

    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
